The annual inflation rate in Canada remained unchanged at 3%, matching market expectations.

According to Statistics Canada, prices at the pump rose 22.8% in August, following a 25.7% increase in the previous month, as the conflict in the Middle East continues to put upward pressure on energy costs.
The Consumer Price Index decreased 0.1% in August from the previous month.
Additionally, grocery prices rose 2.8% in August, down from a 3.1% increase in the previous month, falling below the headline inflation rate for the first time in over two years.

Core inflation rates, which are tracked by the Bank of Canada, remained close to their target. The trimmed-mean core rate and the median core rate were both unchanged at 1.9% and 2%, respectively, aligned with expectations.

title: Canada inflation holds at 3% in August
